title: Interpretable Context Methodology (ICM): Folder Structure as Agent Architecture, Five-Layer Hierarchy, Three Primitives, and Verified Stage Checks
author: Van Clief & McDermott (arXiv:2603.16021, 2026; synthesized by Brain Harness)

source.title: Interpretable Context Methodology: Folder Structure as Agent Architecture

claims.assertion: Folder hierarchy carries context scoping and execution order, replacing complex multi-agent orchestration frameworks with auditable filesystem contracts.
The five-layer context hierarchy (L0 AGENTS.md, L1 root CONTEXT.md, L2 stage CONTEXT.md, L3 factory references, L4 product outputs) bounds per-step agent context to strictly <8,000 tokens.
All production workspaces compose over three core primitives: Sequence (numbered stages, handoffs), Shelf (uniform records), and Catalog (small, stable routing pointers <60 lines).
Every execution step must terminate at an explicit check (person, script, or small model check.md pass/fail) before downstream consumption, arresting error cascades at the earliest boundary.

Restructuring existing legacy codebases into ICM requires non-destructive classification into five file roles (catalog, contract, factory, product, dead) with external referrer verification before moving.

The onboarding questionnaire system uses double-brace SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE placeholders ({{VARIABLE}}) and conditional sections ({{?SECTION}}...{{/SECTION}}) to configure reusable production workspaces without modifying execution logic.
